outcome: No change to the arithmetic (number-field) Bombieri-Lang conjecture as stated in the Wikipedia bullet; all substantial 2024-2026 activity concerns the geometric/function-field analogue, which is a related-but-different problem, not a case or restriction of the number-field statement.

summary: The Wikipedia bullet states the arithmetic Bombieri-Lang conjecture: densities of rational points on algebraic surfaces/varieties over number fields (and their extensions). Searching for progress since 26 January 2024 turns up a genuine cluster of activity, but it is entirely about the *geometric* (function-field) Bombieri-Lang conjecture, a distinct problem posed over function fields rather than number fields. Junyi Xie and Xinyi Yuan (arXiv:2308.08117, submitted Aug 2023, so pre-window) proved the geometric conjecture for varieties with finite morphisms to abelian varieties of trivial trace; Guoquan Gao's Nov 2025 preprint (arXiv:2511.17010, updated Mar 2026) removed the hyperbolicity/non-isotriviality assumptions, extending this to all finite maps to abelian varieties over function fields of characteristic 0; and Junyi Xie's 2026 survey (arXiv:2607.02165) summarizes this cluster of results. I opened all three papers directly (via WebFetch) and confirmed each explicitly frames its result as the 'geometric Bombieri-Lang conjecture ... over function fields,' not the arithmetic/number-field version. Critically, the 2026 survey itself states outright that the arithmetic version (its Conjecture 1.1/2.2) 'remains very open in higher dimension,' explicitly distinguishing it from the now-partially-proved geometric analogue. Under the scope rule (§3.1), the geometric conjecture over function fields is a related problem obtained by changing the base field/setting, not a case obtained by restricting the number-field statement — proving it removes no territory from the arithmetic conjecture Wikipedia's bullet asks about. So none of this counts as progress on the stated problem, and status is 'open' with no_change_found true. On AI: the only AI mention found anywhere in this cluster is in the survey's acknowledgements, thanking an 'AI assistant Xiaozhua' for writing assistance and two people for providing an 'AI-agent environment' that resolved unspecified technical issues — this is writing/infrastructure support, not mathematical content production, so ai_role is 'none' per §6.2. I found no counterexample, disproof, or any other event touching the number-field statement; Terence Tao's blog posts tagged with this conjecture (Erdős-Ulam application, 2014; polynomial bijections, 2019; a related Bresciani preprint, 2021) all predate the window and concern applications assuming the conjecture, not progress toward proving or disproving it.
competing_reading: One could argue that proving the geometric analogue for an important test class (finite covers of abelian varieties) is evidence toward, or a strong heuristic analogue of, the arithmetic statement, since Vojta's dictionary treats the two as parallel conjectures and progress on one sometimes transfers proof techniques to the other. Under a looser reading of scope, a reviewer might code this as 'progress' (a related, structurally analogous problem making headway) rather than 'no_change_found.' I did not adopt this reading because the survey's own authors keep the two conjectures explicitly separate and say the arithmetic one is untouched by this work — the analogy is methodological inspiration, not a mathematical implication.
what_would_settle_it: A statement, by an expert or the original authors, that the geometric-case techniques (Nevanlinna theory / entire-curve constructions) have been shown to transfer to an actual arithmetic (number-field) result — e.g., a new case of the number-field Bombieri-Lang conjecture proved, cited as using ideas from Xie-Yuan/Gao. No such transfer has been reported as of this search.
